sentences.text: Learned counsel for the petitioner has submitted that the petitioner is in no way involved in the offence alleged in the FIR and as he is an old and ailing person, suffering from various multiple joint pain, with deformity of feet bones along with poor vision and is not in a position to visit Guwahati.

However, as the 41A notice has mentioned that the invoices mentioned therein are allegedly in respect of the consignment, therefore, he is apprehending arrest in connection with this case.
7.

Learned counsel for the petitioner has also submitted that considering his health condition, he may be given some time to appear before the Investigating Officer and he is willing to cooperate with the investigation.

8. Learned counsel for the petitioner has also submitted an additional affidavit, and through the Annexure-A, additional affidavit, the learned counsel has substantiated his statement that the petitioner made every endeavour to get his statement recorded by the IO, but his statement could not be recorded by the IO.

9. I have considered the submissions at the Bar with circumspection. .
10.

The petitioner has made every endeavour to get his statement recorded by the IO.
The petitioner is willing to get his statement recorded by the IO by any means and if possible through electronic mode.
